title: Towards High-Performance Transactional Stateful Serverless Workflows with Affinity-Aware Leasing
problem: Serverless platforms struggle to efficiently maintain transactional state consistency across distributed function invocations while achieving high performance, as state coordination typically introduces significant latency overhead and coordination bottlenecks.
motivation: Stateful serverless workflows are increasingly common in practice, but existing systems either sacrifice strong consistency or incur substantial performance penalties.
method: The system uses temporary ownership agreements (called leases) to ensure only one function can modify a piece of data at a time, keeping it consistent. To avoid slowdowns from moving data across the network, it places functions close to the data they need (called affinity-aware placement). By combining these two strategies—leasing for consistency and colocated placement for speed—the system handles many concurrent tasks without corruption or major performance loss.
key_novelty: Use temporary-access leases combined with placing functions near their data to achieve both consistency and speed in serverless systems.
contributions: Affinity-aware leasing protocol for transactional state management in serverless systems
Transactional consistency guarantees with minimal coordination overhead
Scheduler that co-locates functions and state based on affinity awareness
System implementation demonstrating high-performance execution of stateful workflows

metrics.speedup: performance improvement over baseline serverless approaches
